transcript.text: Alright everyone, we've got a ten-business-day stability sprint coming up with capacity for one primary technical-debt focus. Before I lock the plan, I want to run our normal round-robin check-in. We have three candidates on the backlog: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Let's start with backend engineering — what's your perspective on these three?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a security finding before we go further. Minutes ago in the dependency scanner, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was still verifying scanner results and hadn't filed the finding yet, but given Devon just indicated that team is close to finishing that migration, I think this needs to be on the table for this sprint.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something important to add from the customer support side. During a customer call this morning, I confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior. Those accounts will need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. I recorded the call in a support note that hasn't synced to the sprint-planning system yet, so this wouldn't be visible to anyone else right now.
transcript.speaker: A4

Prepare and deliver a migration guide for the 42 enterprise accounts depending on the old audit-column behavior before enabling the new behavior.
Record the sprint plan locking legacy_csv_exporter as the primary technical-debt focus and ensure the planning board is updated with all disclosed findings.
